ai-at-work.title: Everpure sees AI infrastructure strategy move beyond virtual machines
ai-at-work.excerpt: AI infrastructure strategy is expanding beyond compute and storage specifications as artificial intelligence reshapes who manages enterprise applications and data. Infrastructure teams are increasingl
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Everpure is positioning itself as the infrastructure platform that handles the messy reality of AI workloads running alongside traditional IT systems instead of pretending they exist in separate universes. For digital workplace pros, this matters because your infrastructure teams are about to get asked to support everything at once, and pretending the old silos still exist won't cut it anymore. The real test isn't whether Everpure solves this, it's whether any vendor can actually make infrastructure teams' lives simpler instead of just adding another layer of complexity to manage.

ai-at-work.title: Resect launches with $25M to reduce hallucinations in AI models
ai-at-work.excerpt: Seattle-based artificial intelligence research startup Resect AI announced Thursday it has raised $25 million in early funding to build an accountability layer for enterprise AI by capturing and reduc
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Resect AI just grabbed $25 million to tackle AI hallucinations by adding an accountability layer that catches false outputs in real time. For digital workplace folks deploying AI tools, this matters because nothing tanks user trust faster than your chatbot confidently telling someone their expense report is due on the 47th of Octember. If this actually works, it could be the difference between employees embracing AI assistance and abandoning it after the first spectacular confidence-fueled mistake.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Experian and ServiceNow are teaming up to deploy AI agents that embed Experian's data and decision-making tools directly into enterprise workflows. This matters because digital workplace pros are about to see a lot more autonomous agents handling routine customer service and data tasks, which means rethinking how teams interact with these systems and what skills matter most going forward. The real question is whether these agents actually reduce busywork or just create a new layer of complexity that someone has to manage and troubleshoot.

ai-at-work.title: Nvidia bags Hugging Face, AI models play leapfrog and CrowdStrike doubles down on AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Perhaps it’s no surprise that Nvidia ended up embracing open artificial intelligence model archive Hugging Face this week following more than a week of rumors. Even at almost $13 billion, it may end u
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nvidia acquired Hugging Face, the major open-source AI model repository, signaling that big tech is consolidating control over the AI infrastructure that everyone else depends on. This matters because your workplace's ability to experiment with or deploy AI tools just got filtered through fewer gatekeepers, and whatever Nvidia decides to do with that platform will ripple through every organization trying to build their own AI capabilities. At thirteen billion dollars, this is what "we're not really competing anymore, we're just acquiring the game board" looks like.

industry-news.title: Anthropic Wins Back Trump Administration’s Trust After Pentagon Fight
industry-news.excerpt: Anthropic is rebuilding ties with the Trump administration after its Pentagon fight, potentially reopening the door to federal AI contracts. The post Anthropic Wins Back Trump Administration’s Trust A
industry-news.dwp_take: Anthropic patched things up with the Trump administration following a previous dispute over Pentagon contracts, putting federal AI deals back in play. This matters because if AI companies want serious government contracts, they need to stay on the right side of whoever's in charge, and that political calculus directly affects which tech platforms federal workers end up using. Here's the thing though: an AI vendor's ability to land Pentagon work shouldn't depend on whether they smoothed over a political dustup. That's how you end up with mediocre tools because the winner wasn't chosen on merit.

industry-news.title: Agents on the frontline: How Box is using AI to supercharge cybersecurity
industry-news.excerpt: How can enterprises adopt AI agents in a safe and secure manner?
industry-news.dwp_take: Box announced new AI agents designed to help security teams detect and respond to threats faster by automating routine investigation work. For digital workplace pros, this matters because security isn't someone else's problem anymore, it's baked into how we architect collaboration platforms and manage data access. Here's the thing though: every AI security agent is only as good as the humans who set its boundaries, and I've seen plenty of automation theatre where companies deploy AI and then act surprised when it makes decisions nobody fully understands.

industry-news.title: Oracle expands HPE Juniper Networking deal to support AI infrastructure build-out
industry-news.excerpt: The deal is aimed at supporting scale, performance, and availability as Oracle expands its AI superclusters
industry-news.dwp_take: Oracle is doubling down on its partnership with HPE Juniper to beef up networking infrastructure specifically built for AI workloads. This matters because the plumbing that connects your AI systems directly impacts whether your genAI initiatives actually work at scale, and most companies are woefully unprepared on the network side. Here's the thing: everyone's rushing to buy AI tools without realizing their five-year-old network infrastructure is about to become a very expensive bottleneck.

industry-news.title: ‘AI is increasingly becoming operational infrastructure rather than a productivity add-on’: Yesterday’s triple AI outage should be a wake-up call for enterprises
industry-news.excerpt: Greater vendor transparency is needed in the wake of outages at OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI
industry-news.dwp_take: Three major AI services went down simultaneously yesterday, exposing how quickly enterprises have woven these tools into their core operations without proper redundancy or fallback plans. Digital workplace teams now have to answer uncomfortable questions from leadership about whether their AI-dependent workflows can survive a bad day at the vendor's data center. After 30 years watching technology adoptions, I can tell you that betting your company's Monday morning on someone else's infrastructure is how you end up explaining downtime to the board instead of doing actual work.
